opsspec Review
Alpha Category
Alpha One. Primary Business Address. Authorization to operate under part 91. Alpha two. Definitions and abbreviations. Alpha three. Authorized aircraft types. Alpha four. List of authorized op spec paragraphs. Alpha six. List of management personnel. Chief Pilot, Nathan Larson-Alexander. Director of Operations, Darrin Greubel. Director of Maintenance, Buck Curry. Agent for service, Christopher Burns. Alpha seven. List of designated persons. Alpha eight. List of persons with operational control. Consist of the Director of Operations, the Chief Pilot and the Director of Maintenance. Alpha nine. Defines the means by which the certificate holder will obtain, maintain, and distribute aeronautical data for the airports it uses. Located in G.O.M chapter 5 Alpha ten. Approved sources of aviation weather information. Alpha fifteen. Authorization to use an autopilot in lieu of a second in command along with a list of approved autopilot systems. Alpha twenty four. Authorization to perform air ambulance operations. Alpha twenty five. Authorization to use electronic signatures, electronic record keeping systems and electronic manual systems along with a list of approved systems. Alpha twenty seven. Authorization to perform Land and Hold Short Operations. Landing distance should be A.F.M. plus 1000 feet. No wet runways. Runway must have electronic or visual approach guidance. Weather of no less than a 1500 foot ceiling and a visibility of no less than 5 statute miles. Weather can be reduced to 1000 and 3 if a PAPI or VASI is installed and operational. Where a rejected landing procedure is published, weather minima will be published in local flying directives. LAH SO not authorized if wind-shear reported in the 20 minutes prior to the LAH SO clearance. Tailwind should be calm or less than 3 knots. Night LAH SO only with approved LAH SO lighting installed. Alpha thirty one. Authorization to use contract training facilities. Alpha forty one. Authorization to complete a pre-takeoff contamination check. Alpha forty six. Authorization to perform single engine I.F.R. passenger carrying operations. Alpha fifty seven. Authorization to perform eligible on demand operations. Eligible on demand operations will be conducted in accordance with Guardian flight G.O.M. Chapter 9. Alpha sixty one. Authorization to conduct operations using an electronic flight bag, and the aircraft authorized under that program. Alpha ninety six. Authorization to use only actual weights when determining aircraft weight and balance. Solicited weights must be passenger weight plus ten pounds. Alpha three forty eight. Authorization to allow persons eligible under part one twenty one dot five forty seven access to the flight deck using the Cockpit Access security system program and or the flight standards flight deck access restriction program in accordance with the relevant limitations and provisions. Alpha four forty nine. The certificate holder will comply with the requirements of 14 C.F.R. part 120 and 49 C.F.R. part 40 for it's anti drug and alcohol misuse prevention program. Alpha nine nine nine. Copy of the Air operator certificate issued to guardian flight.
Bravo Category
Bravo thirty. Authorization to conduct I.F.R. en route, area navigation operations in the state of Alaska and its airspace, on published air traffic routes using G.P.S. WAAS R-NAV systems, as the only means of I.F.R. navigation, in accordance with the provisions of S-FAR ninety seven and this opsspec. Bravo thirty three. IFR en route operations. This opsspec replaces bravo 31, 32, 34, and 35. Authorizes IFR en route operations using R-NAV and, or, GNSS in areas without ground-based NAVAIDs, requiring the aircraft to maintain at least a One-Hour Reliable Fix (1HRF) capability, or comply with additional operational limitations if it cannot. For the purposes of this opsspec, One Hour Reliable Fix operations are defined as, Operations over land or over water where a reliable ground-based NAVAID fix is available at least once each hour. Bravo forty six. Authorization to conduct operations in reduced vertical separation minimum or R.V.S.M. airspace as well as the relevant requirements and limitations. Bravo fifty. Authorization to conduct en route operations in the listed specific areas as well as the relevant limitations and provisions. Bravo four fifty. Information regarding sensitive international areas as well as any authorizations and the point of contact for any timely updates.
Charlie Category
Charlie fifty one. Authorization to conduct terminal instrument operations. Charlie fifty two. Authorization to conduct specific types of instrument approach procedures as listed in this op spec as well as the relevant limitations and provisions. Charlie fifty four. High minimum P.I.C. provisions and limitations on the use of landing minimums for turbojet airplanes. Charlie fifty five. Authorization to derive alternate airport weather minimums. For airports with at least one operational navigational facility providing a straight in, non precision, or CAT one precision, approach procedure, add 400 feet to the minimum descent altitude or height, or decision altitude or height, and add one statute mile to the landing minimum visibility. For airports with at least two operational navigational facilities each providing a straight in approach procedure to different suitable runways add 200 feet to the higher minimum descent altitude or height, or decision altitude or height and add one half statute mile to the higher landing minimum visibility of the two approaches to be used. If appropriately equipped, you may use a G.P.S. based instrument approach procedures at both the destination and an alternate airport. However, At the alternate, only L-NAV or circling M.D.A.'s are to be planned for unless equipped with ba ro V-NAV. Planning for the use of G.P.S. based instrument approach procedures, must be based on a single navigational facility, when determining the approach facility configuration in Table 1, even if there are two or more G.P.S. approaches to different suitable runways.
Charlie fifty seven. I.F.R. take-off minimums for part one thirty five airplane operations. Standard takeoff minimums are 1 statute mile, or R.V.R 5000, for airplanes having two engines or less, and one half statute mile, or R.V.R 24 hundred, for airplanes having more than 2 engines. Additionally, the certificate holder is authorized to use a takeoff minimum equal to the lowest authorized straight-in Category one I.F.R. landing minimum, applicable to the certificate holder for that particular airport. The touchdown R.V.R report, if available, is controlling. If a higher than standard takeoff minimum is published, and no alternative procedure is prescribed, that higher published takeoff minimum is controlling. The note prohibiting single-engine I.F.R. part one 35 passenger-carrying operations, in lower than standard takeoff minimums, only applies to non turbine single-engine aircraft.
Charlie sixty three. Authorization to conduct I.F.R. R-NAV one and, or, R.N.P. one, departure procedures, standard terminal arrival routes, and or tailored arrivals, using approved R-NAV systems. Charlie sixty four. Authorization to conduct non scheduled passenger and all cargo terminal area I.F.R. operations, in Class Golf airspace, or at airports without an operating control tower, in accordance with the limitations and provisions in this paragraph. Charlie sixty seven. Special authorization, provisions and limitations for certain airports.
Charlie seventy three. Vertical navigation, V-NAV, instrument approach procedures, I.A.P. , using minimum descent altitude, M.D.A. , as a decision altitude, D.A. , or Decision height, D.H. Allows specific aircraft with specific equipment and software to use an M.D.A. as a D.A. or D.H. . This opsspec provides protection for the temporary altitude loss below the MDA when performing a missed approach when using an MDA as a D.A. or D.H. . Simply stated, the runway for the non-precision approach to be used, must also be served by a precision approach with vertical guidance or a visual glide slope indicator. The final approach course must be exactly the same, and the Visual descent angle must be the same or greater. The vertical path flown must cross at or above all step down fix altitudes as referenced on the barometric altimeter. Specific V-NAV path angles are required for different categories of aircraft. If the requirements of this section are not met, the certificate holder may still use a continuous descent final approach, but must begin the missed approach so as not to descend below the M.D.A.
Charlie seventy five. Circle to land approach maneuver, Category One I.F.R. landing minimums. Defines the limitations and provisions under which a circle to land maneuver may be performed, from an instrument approach procedure. Charlie seventy seven. Terminal Visual Flight Rules, limitations, and provisions. Applies to turbojet operations. Charlie seventy nine. I.F.R. lower than standard takeoff minima, 14 C.F.R. part one thirty five airplane operations, all airports. Applies to turbojet operations. Charlie eighty one. Special Instrument and R-NAV visual flight procedures. Contains a list of special instrument approach procedures authorized for use in flight operations.
